reasons: Tier 1: read-only, public or internal data only

summary: This agent is read-only (Tier 1) but has several operational and security gaps: shared credentials, untrusted web inputs without provenance controls, an untested manual kill switch, use of an external model without documented vendor controls, and logs not forwarded to the SIEM. Mitigations should include scoped per-agent credentials, input provenance and sanitization, a tested automated kill switch, vendor risk assessment, and forwarding logs to the SIEM before approving production use.

findings.whyItMatters: A shared token increases risk that a single credential compromise or misuse will affect multiple services and makes auditing attribution and least-privilege enforcement difficult. An attacker who obtains the shared token could use the agent's read access to internal CRM data.
findings.recommendedControl: Issue a scoped, per-agent service credential with the minimum required permissions, rotate it regularly, and enable per-credential auditing and revocation.

findings.whyItMatters: The agent consumes untrusted web content and public sources which can contain misleading, malicious, or adversarially crafted data that the model may incorporate into briefs, producing incorrect or harmful outputs. There is no evidence of input validation, provenance tagging, or sanitization controls.
findings.recommendedControl: Implement input validation and provenance checks: restrict allowed sources, sanitize and annotate web-sourced content with origin metadata, and require the agent to cite source provenance and confidence intervals in its summaries.

findings.evidenceQuote: "killSwitch": {"available": true,"description": "Manual: the on-call engineer disables the agent's service account. No tested runbook."}
findings.whyItMatters: The kill switch is manual and lacks a tested runbook, which could delay disabling the agent during an incident and hinder containment and recovery. Slow or unreliable shutdown procedures reduce operational safety if the agent misbehaves.
findings.recommendedControl: Provide an automated, documented kill switch with a tested runbook and regular drills; ensure the kill action can be executed immediately by authorized personnel and that it disables all active credentials and network access.

findings.whyItMatters: The model depends on an external provider (Anthropic), introducing supply-chain risk from third-party code, model updates, or outages that could change behavior or availability without internal control. There is no documentation of vendor assessment or allowed-model policy.
findings.recommendedControl: Perform a formal vendor security and SLA assessment, specify approved model versions, and establish change-notification and rollback procedures before allowing the external model in production.

findings.evidenceQuote: "logging": {"enabled": true,"destination": "Application logs, not yet forwarded to the SIEM"}
findings.whyItMatters: Application logs are not forwarded to the SIEM, which weakens centralized detection, alerting, and incident response capabilities; malicious or accidental agent behavior may not be detected quickly. This reduces visibility and increases time-to-contain for any compromise or misuse.
findings.recommendedControl: Forward agent logs to the enterprise SIEM with structured, tamper-evident logging, enable alerting for anomalous access or queries, and retain logs per the incident response policy.
